text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementTechnologyWorkers Who Fear AI May be More Prone to Slacking Off“Jobs apocalypse” or not, threats have consequencesJCBy Jake Currie3:30 PM CDT on October 16, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleJust a few years ago, the leaders of major AI companies undertook a rather bizarre public relations strategy to promote their new products—they promised (threatened?) that they’d wipe out entire industries. “Entire classes of jobs will go away and not come back,” OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said in 2019. Now, with public backlash to AI data centers in particular reaching a fever pitch (and an oddly bipartisan one, given how politically polarized we are), tech titans are scrambling to recalibrate. They’re backing off previous claims of a “jobs apocalypse” and promising AI disruption will be much less, well, disruptive. Read more: “Mere Minutes With AI Causes a Sharp Drop in Persistence”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
